query: What advantages and operating requirements does the Spinmatron-2737 multiblock have?

relevant_chunk.text:
[MassProcessing > Spinmatron-2737]
Tired of spamming Centrifuges already? 

Alas, with your newfound ZPM technology you can finally fabricate a Centrifuge with some real power; The Spinmatron-2737!

The Spinmatron comes with a litany of advantages compared to the regular centrifuge multiblock, including a 3x Speed boost, a 30% reduction in EU usage, and a malleable number of parallels.

Unlike the generic turbine that comes stock in a normal Centrifuge, the Spinmatron graciously allows you to choose the quality of the turbines that go into the machine. You can add between 2-8 turbines depending on the machine tier, each turbine will increase the parallel amount by [4 * Turbine Material Tier]. (You'll want to avoid using smaller, non-huge turbines!)

This efficiency comes at a cost however, and will require [Recipe Tier * 10] L/s of Kerosene in order to run. This can optionally be switched out with Biocatalyzed Propulsion Fluid for a 1.25x parallel multiplier once you've reached UEV.

Additionally there are three modes that come unique to the Spinmatron:

- Light -> Gives increased speed in exchange for only being able to process [Voltage Tier - 3] recipes

- Normal -> No changes

- Heavy -> Grants the ability to craft Heavy Mode dependent recipes in exchange for reducing your parallels by 32x and consuming Biocatalyzed Propulsion Fluid.

[note]Checkout the tooltip for more information![/note]

[warn]Use the GUI for adding turbines; don't add them to the rotor assemblies.[/warn]

Required items: gregtech:gt.blockmachines:1033 x1, gregtech:gt.blockcasings12:9 x709, SC Turbine Casing x264, PBI Pipe Casing x160, gregtech:gt.blockglass1:6 x144, bartworks:BW_TieredGlass x81, Block of Naquadah Alloy x56, IsaMill Gearbox x54, Turbine Shaft x24, Pikyonium 64B Frame Box x9, Rotor Assembly x8

Rewards: Chrom Dust

query: Which alloys require the Alloy Blast Smelter and how does input separation work on it?

relevant_chunk.text:
[Alloy Blast Smelter > Usage + Trivia]
The ABS smelts dusts into molten alloys. Many of the basic alloys can also be made in the Industrial Mixing Machine and Zyngen, but it is typically faster and more efficient to smelt them directly into fluids in the ABS. Tougher alloys such as indalloy 140 or maraging steel can only be made in the ABS, which gates many of the other IV tier multiblocks. There are no tiered components or any sort of bonuses and there is no tier skipping, even when overclocking with multiple energy hatches.

Input separation should be enabled on the ABS to prevent SOLID ingredients in different input buses from being used in the same recipe, including any programmed circuits. That means a single ABS with many input buses can support many different programmed circuits simultaneously. Just don't forget to stay above the minimum number of casings. FLUID ingredients are always shared regardless of input separation, unless the input hatch is colored.

{{ABSRecipes}}

Trivia:
* The programmed circuit for ABS recipes is generally tied to the number of inputs instead of actually preventing recipe conflicts.
relevant_chunk.title: Alloy Blast Smelter

query: What happens to excess power in the Active Transformer and does it explode when hot-swapping components?

relevant_chunk.text:
[Active Transformer > Usage]
The AT receives power from energy hatches and outputs power via dynamo hatches, similar to the Lapotronic Supercapacitor. The voltage and amperage does NOT matter. For example, an AT can have one 16,384A UEV laser target hatch as input and sixteen 1,024A UV laser source hatches as output. Excess power is neither consumed nor voided. However, there is a 0.004% power loss for all EU that passes through the machine, which is practically negligible except when the demand/consumption is 100% of the total input. Don't forget that there is also a max amperage/s power loss for each laser source hatch.

The AT is very forgiving when it comes to hot-swapping components. The machine does NOT explode and even provides a grace period of at least 60 seconds before the structure unforms. However, breaking energy hatches voids any power stored in their buffer.
relevant_chunk.title: Active Transformer

query: What is the optimal output hatch fill percentage for maximum growth and productivity in the Bacterial Vat?

relevant_chunk.text:
[Bacterial Vat > Overview]
(Name: Bacterial Vat, Source: [https://github.com/GTNewHorizons/GT5-Unofficial/blob/master/src/main/java/bartworks/common/tileentities/multis/MTEBioVat.java GregTech5u], Type: Bacterial Vat, Tier: HV, Size: 5 x 5 x 4, Energyhatches: Regular, Overclocks: Imperfect, Pollution: None)

The Bacterial Vat (BV) is an HV tier multiblock for mass fermenting fluids. Bacteria contained within the vat break down organic compounds into something new, such as Saccharomyces Escherichia turning grape juice into wine. The species of bacteria, and therefore the recipe, is determined by placing a petri dish with a culture inside the controller block of the machine. All cultures are made in the Biolab singleblock machine. Some more exotic and alien species of bacteria require radiation to survive which is supplied through a radio hatch containing radioactive materials. The fermenting process itself is closely tied to the carrying capacity of the environment, meaning the output hatch should stay as close as possible to 50% capacity for maximum growth and productivity. Although the BV is mandatory for progression in UV, the player can later craft all the necessary fluids in the Quantum Force Transformer.
relevant_chunk.title: Bacterial Vat

query: Where in the crafting grid must a Tinkers Construct tool be placed when repairing it in an adventure backpack or crafting station?

relevant_chunk.text:
[Tinkers Tools > Repairs]
A TiC tool may be repaired by combining it with the base form of the head's material in a tool station, tool forge, crafting station, or adventure backpack. For example, repair an iron pickaxe head with an iron ingot. The tool must be placed in the center of the crafting grid (on the pickaxe icon) for the crafting station and adventure backpack specifically. Larger repairs may be made by adding more ingots to the surrounding grid slots. The total durability restored depends on the amount of materials used, the base durability of the tool before modifiers, a multiplier that decreases with the number of previous repairs, and a multiplier that increases with the number of unused modifiers, as seen in the following equation.

<math>\text{Durability Restored} = \text{Ingots} \times (50 + 0.8 \times \text{Base Durability}) \times \text{Repair Multiplier} \times \text{Modifier Multiplier}</math>
The repair multiplier is increased every time the tool is repaired which means additional repairs restore 1% less durability down to a minimum of 50%. It is highly recommended to make larger repairs with more materials because they only increase the number of repairs by one for the whole operation. At best, each ingot or base material restores over 80% of the tool's base durability. At worst, each ingot or base material restores slightly over 28% of the tool's base durability.
<math>\text{Repair Multiplier} = \text{Max}(0.5, (100 - \text{Repair Count})/100)</math>

| Unused Modifiers | Modifier Multiplier |
| --- | --- |
| 3+ | 1.0 |
| 2 | 0.9 |
| 1 | 0.8 |
| 0 | 0.7 |
relevant_chunk.title: Tinkers Tools

query: Why does the mining level shown in the NEI Tool Materials tab differ from the extruder and smeltery tabs?

relevant_chunk.text:
[Tinkers Tools > Levels > Mining Level]
A tool's mining level determines what blocks it can break. The WAILA tooltip displays the mining level requirement (ie. 05-Obsidian) while looking at a block. The text appears green if the current tool meets the requirement, or red if it does not. Mining level is only present on tools that break stone/ore blocks like Pickaxes and Hammers.

Mining level can be increased ONE time by earning enough mining XP. See the tooltip of a tool for its current mining XP and the required amount to level-up. Replacing a tool head resets the mining XP back to zero. After leveling-up, the mining XP reads "Boosted" to indicate that it cannot be increased any further. The NEI Tool Materials tab always shows the boosted mining level of a material, but the extruder and smeltery tabs always show the unboosted mining level.

Mining level can also be instantly boosted by having an item (Zombie Head 1, Skeleton Skull 2, Creeper Head 4, Wither Skull 7, or Nether Star 8) added to it. Each item only works on tools up to the mining level listed on the head and shows on the tool's icon. These items do not cost a modifier slot to apply but can only be added to fully repaired tools.
{{Important|All mining levels on this page are the BOOSTED mining levels. New tools and parts are always going to start one level down until enough mining XP has been earned.}}
relevant_chunk.title: Tinkers Tools

query: How can Forestry tree saplings be obtained using tools and bees?

relevant_chunk.text:
[Tree Breeding > Obtaining Saplings]
Forestry applies genetics to trees the same way it does to Bees. Vanilla tree saplings can be analyzed with the Field Kit, Scanner (GT) or Treealyzer, or collected from fertilized leaf blocks with a Grafter or Branch Cutter. Lumberjack villagers also can offer a single trade for a random Forestry sapling of any type, and chests in Forestry village houses may have random saplings. Any type of Bee with the Flower: Flowers trait can pollinate trees inside it's Territory x3 (default Average is 9x9 footprint, six blocks tall, so 27x27x18 for tree pollination), which will result in Forestry saplings. Butterflies also pollinate and will spawn naturally from Forestry-analyzed trees, but are much slower and less predictable at the job than bees are.

Forestry saplings can be accelerated with watering cans, bonemeal and other methods just like their vanilla counterparts. Oak converts to "Apple Oak", Spruce to "Red Spruce" and Birch to "Silver Birch", but other than the name change the tree appearance remains the same.
relevant_chunk.title: Tree Breeding

query: Which GregTech tools are exceptions to the standard material scaling for durability and mining speed?

relevant_chunk.text:
[GT Tools > Recommended Materials]
The following table is a list of recommended materials that maximize durability and/or mining speed for GT Tools. These values are generally shared between all types of tools. One exception is the electric wrench which applies a multiplier depending on the voltage tier (up to 4x for HV). Another exception is the soft mallet which scales with completely different materials.

Note that the Vajra is unlocked in IV and is perfect for breaking blocks, machines, pipes, wires, etc. It has infinite durability, speed, and even a silk touch mode for higher precision. However, the Vajra cannot change the direction of pipes/wires, toggle multiblock settings, or repair maintenance issues; the standard GT tools are still needed for those tasks.

query: Which mod manages the Dungeonchest.xml loot table in GTNH?

relevant_chunk.text:
[DungeonChest Loot Table > Overview]
Dungeonchest.xml is a file that controls Loot distribution. In vanilla, it's responsible for seeding the mossy cobblestone square dungeons with single spawners. In GT:NH, this table is managed by TooMuchLoot and has a greatly expanded pool of items to draw from. In addition to the basic vanilla dungeon, dungeonChest populates Webbed Greatwoods and Hilltop Stones hazard chests. Separate tables are used for Lootgames, Mineshafts and Strongholds.
